info.title: looot API
info.description: Discover, inspect, run, and pay for real (or fixture) provider operations through one bearer token.

get.summary: Discover operations
Paged, filtered, faceted catalog listing

200.description: Catalog listing page with nextCursor and, when facets=true, category/platform/provider/capability counts for the filtered set

get.summary: Ranked full-text catalog search, with capability expansion and a stemmed-token fallback so a long natural-language query is never empty
get.description: The same search core answers MCP `search` (10 title rows by default) and MCP search_catalog (50 full rows by default, like this route). A title row is a subset of this route's row: endpointId, provider, name, capability, category, estimatedPrice, priceBasis, access, executionMode, costPerSuccessUsd (facts.costPerSuccessUsd), async (facts.async), works, sourceCapability and credential, in the same order for the same q, limit and offset for a customer token. A platform operator token differs: this route always includes unavailable rows, while MCP honors an explicit filters.includeUnavailable false.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where the page starts in the ranked list; pass the previous page's nextOffset (null on the last page).

parameters.name: mock
parameters.description: true/false excludes the other kind; omitted keeps both but real providers still rank above mocks

parameters.name: prefer
parameters.description: How providers are ordered inside a job: balanced (default), cheapest, reliable or fastest. Any other value is a 400 validation_error. Every item's facts carry it and the body echoes it; it changes the order only once the gateway serves the shared ranking.

200.description: Ranked catalog items (each carrying mock, verified, keyless, runnableNow, stats, access, matchedBy, facts, works, credential and sourceCapability; capability is the resolved job id), same shape as the listing, plus the prefer value used. An empty page may carry warnings (no_supply_for_job) or priceHint (price_above_max: maxPriceMicros removed every endpoint that does the named job; it names the cheapest)

get.summary: What the catalog covers: categories > platforms > jobs with provider, endpoint and runnable counts
get.description: Publicly readable without a bearer token; the same answer for every caller, rebuilt only when the catalog revision (or a platform key or fee) changes. Counts the rows the live public catalog lists (GET /v1/public-catalog when it serves the live catalog): the same row rules and public record checks (hidden slugs, prohibited, mock, unpriced, inactive and disabled rows, and records the public schema refuses, are left out). A category is the vocabulary category of the job's platform, `other` when the platform is not in the vocabulary. Every level (category, platform, job) carries providerCount (distinct providers), endpointCount, runnableCount (runnable without your own key: keyless, or a platform key exists), cheapestPerCall and cheapestPerResult (lowest prices, the price you pay, null when nothing is priced that way; never compared with each other). The default answer is depth summary (totals plus one entry per category, a few KB); depth=full is the whole document (about 490 KB). category or platform narrows to one branch (default depth platforms; depth=jobs lists its jobs) and then answers filter instead of totals. topic answers the matching jobs, at most 25. Each view has its own ETag; revalidate with If-None-Match.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: summary (default): totals and per category counts. platforms: adds each category's platforms. jobs: adds each platform's jobs (a tree). full: each category's platforms[] and flat jobs[] with job.platform. Default platforms when category or platform is given; pass jobs to list the branch jobs. Not allowed with topic.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: A category id: answers only that category. Unknown: 404 unknown_category.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: A platform id: answers the category holding it with only that platform. Unknown (or not in the given category): 404 unknown_platform.

parameters.name: topic
parameters.description: Words such as email or phone: answers the jobs whose id, title, platform or category match (the job-first search matcher), best first, at most 25, with truncated. Combines with category and platform.

200.description: Catalog overview view: a depth view, or a topic view when topic is given

400.description: validation_error: error.field names the argument (depth, category, platform or topic) and error.message says what to send

404.description: unknown_category (error.categories lists the ids) or unknown_platform; error.field names the argument

503.description: catalog_loading: no catalog snapshot is loaded yet; retry after retry-after seconds. production_runtime_unavailable: this deployment serves no v2 catalog

post.summary: Create a run -- idempotencyKey replay returns the existing run (any status) with replayed:true instead of creating a new one
post.description: customer-test friction #4 (docs/product/reviews/2026-09-04-customer-test): dispatch is woken immediately for the run's workspace rather than left for the next poll tick, and the run always returns immediately unless `wait` asks otherwise (either as this query parameter or as a body field of the same name -- the query parameter wins if both are given). `wait=true` (or a bare `?wait`) waits up to the default of 20 s; a number is seconds, clamped to [0, 60]. Returns the result inline, in the same run shape this endpoint already returns, once it reaches a terminal status within `wait` seconds. If it is still queued/running when the window ends, returns that queued/running run instead, exactly as with no `wait` at all -- poll it with GET /v1/runs/{runId} or runs_get. A 201 can carry status:"failed" (a pre-dispatch denial such as endpoint_not_found or a validation_error) -- check the run's own `status` and `error` fields, never the HTTP status code alone, to know whether it actually ran.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a terminal result inline (default 20 when true/bare, max 60). Omit entirely for the pre-existing immediate-return behavior.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Alternative to the request body's idempotencyKey field. Either satisfies the (still mandatory) requirement; if both are present, they must be equal or the request is a 400.

201.description: Run created (or the existing run replayed, any status, with replayed:true). A 201 is not itself success -- a pre-dispatch denial (endpoint_not_found, validation_error) also answers 201 with status:"failed" and a populated error; read the body, not the status code.

402.description: Out of balance -- the run was blocked before dispatch, never billed

409.description: Idempotency-key conflict -- a request already exists for this key that this one does not match

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (execute class, too_many_inflight_runs) -- see Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* response headers

get.summary: Get a run -- on a failed run, error carries { code, providerStatus, message, requestId, whoseError, retryable, retryHint }, never secrets or raw provider headers
get.description: 2026-09-27 (additive): a completed run can carry an optional `normalized` object next to `result`: { job, endpointId, fields, missing, ambiguous, unmapped, providerValues, verdict, verdictReason, mapVerified }, with fixed field names per job and one email status vocabulary (valid, invalid, catch_all, risky, unknown). Present only when the gateway has it turned on and the answering endpoint has an output map; absent, never null, otherwise. `result` and `outcome` are unchanged.

get.summary: Download a stored audio, image, video or PDF result of a run (bytes with the stored content-type; 404 media_not_found, 410 media_expired)
Download a run's stored media through a short-lived signed link, no bearer token
get.description: Unauthenticated: the link itself is the credential. When the gateway has signed media URLs turned on, a run result's `media` (and each `mediaFiles` entry) carries `downloadUrl` next to `downloadPath`: an absolute URL to this route whose query holds `workspace`, `expires` (unix seconds), `v` (1) and `signature` (HMAC-SHA256 over version, workspace, run, media id and expiry). It expires after 15 minutes by default (at most 1 hour, never after the media's own expiresAt). Anyone holding the URL can download the file until it expires, so never put it in logs, analytics or shared transcripts; fetch a fresh run (GET /v1/runs/{runId}) for a new one. Every refusal (bad, expired or tampered link, another workspace or run, unknown or expired media) is the same 404 media_not_found. Off, this path needs a bearer like any other and is not a route.

200.description: The stored bytes with their content-type; cache-control private, no-store; referrer-policy no-referrer

404.description: media_not_found: the link is invalid, expired or tampered, or the media is unknown or expired

post.summary: Register one endpoint directly as data -- no candidate/compatibility-gate/activation-bundle review required
post.description: TP-CAT-10. Creates the provider if it does not exist yet (provider.displayName required in that case). Idempotent by content digest: registering the identical endpoint again is a no-op (created: false); a changed one appends a new version and supersedes the previous active one. When endpoint.capability is not a known canonical job id or alias, the response's capabilitySuggestions lists the closest canonical jobs by name/description match; pass autoCapability: true to register under the top suggestion automatically once its score clears the confidence threshold (default: register exactly the capability submitted).

The platform secret itself is never in this body -- set it via PUT /v1/platform-keys/{providerId}. Submitting oauth2 as the active authMethod is rejected ("oauth2 not available yet"). Body: ProviderDefinitionSchema (src/domain/provider-definition.ts) minus the immutable providerId.

endpointId.description: The catalog endpoint id to run

input.description: Arbitrary key/value input, validated against the endpoint's own input schema

idempotencyKey.description: Required, unless supplied instead as the Idempotency-Key request header (either satisfies the requirement; supplying both requires them to match, or the request is a 400). A replay with the same key and the same body returns the original run (replayed:true); the same key with a different body is a 409. Never auto-generated by the gateway -- see the report's decision options for why.

output.description: Optional output selection/mapping pin; same shape as an inspected endpoint's outputMappingPin

wait.description: Optional alternative to the ?wait= query parameter (the query parameter wins if both are given)

fallback.description: Optional. Let the run move to the next provider of the same job when one misses or fails, within ONE hold; only attempts that ran are charged. true takes every default. The run then carries `route` {servedBy, outcome, chargedUsd, capped, attempts[], skipped[], summary}.

enabled.description: false turns it off (the same as omitting fallback)

maxCostUsd.description: The route's cap; default the sum of the first maxAttempts prices; can only lower it

prefer.description: Order of the job's other providers, default balanced

exclude.description: Endpoint or provider ids never tried

stopAtFirstMiss.description: Stop at the first empty answer, default false

deploymentMode.description: Operator-facing deployment mode: fixture_demo/authenticated_sandbox in local_alpha, approved_production in production, degraded whenever live readiness fails regardless of mode.

role.description: The resolved principal's organization role; null for a resolver that never set one.

expiresAt.description: Present only for ?include=expiresAt: the presenting token's own expiry (ISO 8601 UTC), or null when it has none.

organizationName.description: Present only for ?include=organizationName: the organization's display name, or null when the gateway could not read one.

chain.description: Self-consistency of the currently stored contiguous chain only; not proof against suffix truncation or complete-history rewrite.

unsuppliedJobs.description: Sent only with signals=1 and together with warnings: best-matching job ids no public endpoint is filed under

warnings.description: Sent only with signals=1, when no public endpoint does the query's job; items is then empty

filter.description: Present only on a narrowed view (category or platform given); such a view has no totals

totals.description: Whole catalog; only on a view that is not narrowed

providerCount.description: Distinct providers with at least one listed endpoint at this level

runnableCount.description: Endpoints runnable without your own key (keyless, or a platform key exists)

cheapestPerCall.description: Lowest per-call price in dollars at this level (the price you pay); null when nothing is priced per call

cheapestPerResult.description: Lowest per-result price in dollars at this level (the price you pay); null when nothing is priced per result

inputSchema.description: Draft 2020-12 input schema resolved from fixture, activation bundle, or direct registration; null when the endpoint declares none

requestBinding.description: How validated input fields become the HTTP request (path/query/header/body); null for a fixture or bundle-published endpoint that declares none

uiSchema.description: Presentation hints for a generated form; never validation

outputFormat.description: The endpoint's stored output format, present only when one is stored. Check provenance.verified before relying on it: false means an expected shape not yet checked against real answers

schema.description: Draft 2020-12 output schema, structure only; its $comment says where it came from

validatedAnswers.description: Real saved answers that matched the schema

checkedAnswers.description: Real saved answers the schema was checked against

verified.description: True only when at least one real answer was checked and every one matched

note.description: One-line label, e.g. "validated on 12 real answers" or "expected shape, not yet checked against real answers"

authentication.description: Bearer placeholder only; never contains a credential

examples.description: Equivalent REST, MCP, and CLI requests using placeholders only

scopes.description: Granted scopes, populated after oauth callback or a probe that reports scopes

pendingCredentialRoles.description: Declared secondary credential roles not yet supplied; non-empty implies status action_required

testState.description: verified requires at least one persisted fixture_tested receipt; never set from CRUD alone

probeConfigured.description: true when POST /v1/connections/{connectionId}/probe has a live health check to run; false for a pasted api_key with no probe (the probe then answers 400 validation_error with reason connection_probe_not_configured)

latestTestReceipt.description: Present only in the GET /v1/connections list response (absent, not null, on register/rotate/revoke/etc. responses); the same object GET /v1/connections/{connectionId}/test-receipts returns as `latest`

RegisterConnection.description: One of api_key (default when kind is omitted), oauth, service_account, credential_file, signed_request, or cli_auth, discriminated by kind

secondaryCredentialRoles.description: Secondary credential roles this provider requires beyond the primary auth

resources.description: Accessible provider resource ids discovered by this probe (CA-CONN-03)

remediation.description: Safe human-readable next step; never credential material

keyHint.description: The secret's last 4 characters only; never the secret itself

authConfig.description: How the credential is injected at run time; null falls back to a header/query default derived from the endpoint's own authPlacement

runnable.description: True when a run with no customer connection would actually use this key right now: approved, priced, a secret is stored, and the config can be applied to the provider's endpoints

authMethod.description: Selects which of headerName/paramName/valuePrefix/fields apply; omitted falls back to the endpoint's own authPlacement default

fields.description: Required (at least one) when authMethod is "multi" -- the secret is a JSON object of named fields, each independently placed

PatchPlatformKey.description: Same fields as SetPlatformKey minus secret -- every field optional, only the ones present are changed. Requires an existing platform key for this provider (nothing to reuse a vault ref from otherwise).

authMethod.description: Selects which of headerName/paramName/valuePrefix/fields apply; omitted keeps the existing authConfig

fields.description: Required (at least one) when authMethod is "multi"

providerCalled.description: Always false for this local-fixture-only endpoint; a real provider call happens only through /probe

message.description: Safe status text without credential or provider response material

mapping.description: Strict typed provider mapping; validated for identity, capability, auth, JSON Schemas, effect, price, retry, errors, limits, retention and a disabled fixed-host executor.

RegisterDirectEndpoint.description: provider is optional when :providerId already exists; required (displayName at minimum) when it does not. See DirectEndpointRegistrationInputSchema in src/import/direct-endpoint-registration-service.ts for the full endpoint shape (capability, name, description, executionMode, eligibility, authType, price, and optionally inputSchema/requestBinding/uiSchema/httpContract).

endpoint.description: { endpointId, capability, name, description, executionMode, eligibility, authType, price, inputSchema?, requestBinding?, uiSchema?, httpContract?, examples?, effectClassification? }

autoCapability.description: When endpoint.capability is not a known canonical job id or alias, register under the top capabilitySuggestions match once its score clears the confidence threshold, instead of the exact slug submitted. Default false.

items.description: Same shape as RegisterDirectEndpoint, plus providerId inline.

inputSchema.description: Draft 2020-12 object schema without external references

outputSchema.description: Draft 2020-12 canonical object schema without external references

items.description: Distinct-provider endpoint adapter with contiguous priority, USD ceiling, bounded canonical input/output bindings and explicit miss predicate
